(eqToIso (finiteTypeSpecialization_obj r k) ≪≫
        baseChangeCoordinateSpecialLinearIso r k ≪≫
        eqToIso (SpecialLinear.finiteTypeCoordinateHopfAlgebra_obj k (r + 1)).symm).hom := by
findings.problem: The @[simp] lemma rewrites `(iso).hom.hom` into the whole definition body, written as `.hom` of a `≪≫` chain of isos. That RHS is not a simp normal form. `Iso.trans_hom` and `eqToIso.hom` can fire on it, so simp turns it into a composite of `eqToHom`s and `(baseChangeCoordinateSpecialLinearIso r k).hom`. Because the lemma also unfolds the definition, it exposes the proof-internal construction instead of a stable interface. It also duplicates the definition text, so a change to the definition has to be mirrored in this lemma. The existing simp lemma `mkQuotient_comp_baseChangeCoordinateSpecialLinearIso_hom` shows the intended style: a characterising equation stated through the quotient map. The LHS is a specific `.hom.hom` projection of a subtype-style `isoMk`, so the lemma applies only in narrow situations.
findings.proposed_change: State the lemma with a simp-normal RHS, for example `(finiteTypeSpecializationSpecialLinearIso r k).hom.hom = eqToHom (finiteTypeSpecialization_obj r k) ≫ (baseChangeCoordinateSpecialLinearIso r k).hom ≫ eqToHom (…).symm`. Better still, give a compatibility lemma against `CommHopfAlgCat.mkQuotient` and `SpecialLinear.coordinateMap`, which would be a canonical simp lemma. Alternatively drop @[simp] and keep the lemma as an unfolding lemma used with `rw`.
findings.benefit: Users who simp with the iso would get a predictable `eqToHom ≫ baseChange… ≫ eqToHom` form, or a clean statement in terms of the quotient and coordinate maps. They would not get an unfolded definition body that simp rewrites in a second step. This also removes the duplication between the definition and its simp lemma.
